clue.text: Assail the directors, the doctor included

indicators.note: the doctor is included, taken inside, within the directors' word

parts.note: a company's directors sit together as its board
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the company board, the medic among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack hard, as artillery pounds a position.

clue.text: Tom's mad scene

parts.note: Tom o' ... was a wandering madman named after London's old asylum, a place of chaotic uproar

explanation.surface: A character called Tom has an insane episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethlem Hospital in London was the old asylum whose nickname gave the word for chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The old London madhouse's name came to mean any scene of wild confusion and uproar.

clue.text: Sums are cooked — he manipulates the figures

indicators.note: cooked figures are falsified, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fiddled accounts by a man who massages the numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages works on people's bodies, their figures.

clue.text: Dodging eggs thrown up. I jump about

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means the eggs' word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: ova are eggs
to dance is to jump about

explanation.surface: Avoiding eggs hurled upward, I leap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging something is evading it, which is the act of avoidance.

clue.text: Betrayal of a score of Romans

definitions.meaning: a treacherous deceit of a supposed ally
twenty in Roman numerals is XX, a pair of crosses

explanation.definitionFit: Treachery against one's own side is the double-dealing word, and XX is literally two crosses.

clue.text: A god hears our prayer for support

indicators.note: the listener hears the plea spoken, so its sound is what gets entered

parts.note: a plea for support is 'back us'

explanation.surface: A deity listens to worshippers asking for his backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman deity of wine, so he is an example of a god.

clue.text: Note sounded by a busybody

indicators.note: the musical letter is sounded, spoken aloud, and the sound spelt out

parts.note: B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A tone produced by a meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy bee is proverbially industrious, so the insect is a crossword busybody.

clue.text: The fashion for one in church to act differently

definitions.text: The fashion for one in church

indicators.note: the letters of to act are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's style lets them behave unusually.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short white surplice worn by clergy and choristers, a garment fashioned for church.

clue.text: Plucky Minstrel Boy going to war

definitions.text: Plucky Minstrel Boy going to war

parts.words: Plucky Minstrel Boy going to war
parts.note: Thomas Moore's song 'The Minstrel Boy to the war is gone' has the boy with his wild harp slung behind him; plucky hints at plucking strings

explanation.surface: A brave young singer heads off to battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Moore's minstrel boy carries a harp, so he is a player who plucks one.

clue.text: So death may come in some sporting play-offs

definitions.text: So death may come in some sporting play-offs

parts.words: So death may come in some sporting play-offs
parts.note: a sudden-death play-off ends at the first score, so death arrives abruptly

explanation.surface: Mortality may strike in a sports tie-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden-death decider ends the instant one side scores, without warning.

clue.text: Licentious souls in torment engulfed in turbulent tide

indicators.note: one set of letters is swallowed up inside the other set
turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of tide are stirred into a new order
souls in torment writhe, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Damned spirits suffering, swallowed by a rough sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'turbulent' and 'in torment' are anagram signals, one per word; 'engulfed in' sets the jumbled souls inside the jumbled tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissolute person lives without moral restraint, which is what licentious describes.

clue.text: It changed colour like milady's hair

indicators.note: the two letters of It are changed round into a new order

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something altered its shade, like a lady's dyed hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns IT into TI. 'Tire' is an old verb for dressing the hair (Jezebel 'tired her head' in the Bible), so a fine lady's hair was tired.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage hair that has been dressed or adorned is said to be tired, from attire.

clue.text: The way of progress for each person

definitions.meaning: progress means moving forward, to the front
so much per head, written as two words, a head

explanation.definitionFit: Moving forward is going in front, and 'a head' means one per person, as in five pounds a head.

clue.text: I've pursued one in modern race after fortune — no end profitable

indicators.note: after places the rat second, following the shortened fortune
I've comes after, chasing, the rat
the word for fortune loses its final letter

parts.note: fortune means luck
a competitor in the modern rat race is a rat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has chased a rival in today's rat race, ending up profitable after luck nearly ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: The rat race is the competitive struggle of modern working life, so a rat is one taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lucrative brings in money, so it is profitable.

clue.text: Scripture guide can maybe get into supersonic plane

indicators.note: the scrambled can gets into, enters, the plane's name

parts.note: Concorde was the Anglo-French supersonic airliner

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of can are only possibly in this order

explanation.surface: A tin might be taken aboard the supersonic jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal on 'can'; 'get into' puts the result inside the airliner's name, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical concordance is an alphabetical index of every word in the Bible, a reference aid to it.

clue.text: Idle chatter of this kind advocated by Bunthorne

definitions.text: Idle chatter of this kind advocated by Bunthorne

parts.words: Idle chatter of this kind advocated by Bunthorne
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience the poet Bunthorne sings that meaning does not matter if it is idle chatter of a certain mystic, high-flown kind

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan aesthete recommends empty, lofty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunthorne's song praises talk of a mystical, beyond-experience kind, the exact adjective Gilbert uses.

clue.text: Oriental girl borne shoulder-high

parts.note: E, east, is the oriental direction
Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Eastern young woman is carried aloft on shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is an ornamental strap worn on the shoulder of a uniform.

clue.text: Alias Azariah, retired and gone to pieces

parts.note: one who has retired for the night is in bed

indicators.note: the letters of gone go to pieces and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A man with another name has gone to bed and fallen apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Daniel, Azariah is renamed by the Babylonians; 'to pieces' makes NEGO from GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel 1:7 says Azariah was given a Babylonian name, the one he is known by in the fiery furnace story.

clue.text: A seaman returning from university?

parts.note: an able seaman is AB; turned round it is BA, the degree a graduate brings home from university

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home after studying.
explanation.walkthrough: AB (able seaman) read backwards gives BA, the abbreviation of the degree, so the sailor 'returning' is the graduate's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The BA is the first degree awarded by a university in arts subjects.

clue.text: Church holds dance raised for one of the family

indicators.note: the church letters hold the other piece between them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the dance's word is read upward

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A church puts on an upbeat dance for a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suits a down clue, where the dance reads upward; 'holds' puts it between the two letters for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognate is a blood relation, a kinsman descended from a common ancestor.

clue.text: Cat taking over this game, we hear?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: we hear the word spoken, and its sound is what gets entered

parts.note: in cricket the bowler is the player who takes an over

explanation.surface: A cat takes charge in a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls delivered by one bowler. A tombola is a raffle drawn from a revolving drum, popular at British fetes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tombola is a lottery game with prizes drawn from a drum.

clue.text: Walrus left little to cat

parts.note: morse is an old name for the walrus

explanation.surface: A walrus leaves a scrap of food behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small mouthful of food.

clue.text: Having lined up about one thousand dollars, went astray

indicators.note: the lining-up word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: soldiers who have lined up in rank have dressed
I is the Roman numeral one
a grand, G, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Someone who queued up with a thousand bucks lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is a drill term for lining troops up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject, to stray off course.

clue.text: How the freeborn praise their mother?

definitions.text: How the freeborn praise their mother?

parts.words: How the freeborn praise their mother?
parts.note: the verb for praising highly splits as ...-..., a playful form for those born free of tolls or dues

explanation.surface: A question about how free citizens honour their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise lavishly.

clue.text: Dance next-door to Hell

definitions.meaning: a Caribbean dance under a lowered bar
in Catholic theology the region on the border of Hell for unbaptised souls

explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a bending dance under a pole, and theology's limbo lies on Hell's edge, its neighbour.

clue.text: Play as MPs do

definitions.meaning: to act out a part on stage

explanation.definitionFit: Actors perform a role, and a parliament makes a bill into law; one verb covers both.

clue.text: Atrocious Great War scene, disorderly routs

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of an early First World War battle

indicators.note: the routs are disorderly, so their letters run in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A dreadful First World War battlefield, with armies fleeing in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monstrous is shockingly wicked, which is what atrocious describes.

clue.text: Wipe the floor with member outside the ring

indicators.note: the member's letters go outside, around, the ring

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Thrash a parliamentarian beyond the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop the floor is to wipe it clean, so mop is a synonym for wiping a floor.

clue.text: Go beyond the edge having finished the circuit

parts.note: when something has finished it is over
one circuit of a track is a lap

explanation.surface: A racer runs past the line after completing the course.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to extend past the boundary of something else, covering part of it.

clue.text: I said 17 pounds for the orb

indicators.note: the word I is spoken, and its sound is spelt out

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
17 across is the degree whose abbreviation is BA
LL, doubled L from the Latin librae, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: Someone names seventeen pounds as the price of a globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Orb is a poetic word for the eye, its round ball.
